subject: Clarify: KV cache, streaming fragments, and default retention behavior
messages:
From: Lee Park <lee.park@acmeinc.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on what you keep by default (KV cache, streaming, attachments)

Hi Grace,

Quick follow-up from our security review: can you confirm exactly what Redwood stores by default for hosted API calls? We have a few specific items where our compliance folks want clarity:

- Are KV cache contents ever written to logs or retained beyond the immediate inference session?
- For streaming responses (partial tokens sent to clients), do you store the streamed fragments or only the final assembled response?
- Do function call arguments, file uploads referenced in a session, or binary attachments show up in request/response logs?
- What's the default retention window for request/response logs and prompt inputs/outputs on the hosted plan?

We just need the specifics so we can map to our internal retention policies. If you prefer a short call, happy to sync — cc'ing our infra team.

Thanks,
Lee
Senior Platform Security
Acme Inc

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Lee Park <lee.park@acmeinc.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on what you keep by default (KV cache, streaming, attachments)

Lee — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise breakdown you can share with your compliance team. I kept bullets to make mapping easy.

Summary (hosted API default behavior) — what we store by default:

- Request inputs (prompts): stored as full request payloads to enable debugging, billing, and quality monitoring.
- Final responses (outputs): stored as the complete response record. For streaming calls we persist the assembled final response; transient partial fragments are buffered during streaming but the final assembled output is what is stored for the audit log.
- Streaming fragments: not retained as separate partials by default — only the final document is stored in logs.
- Function call metadata & arguments: stored in the request/response record unless masked by the customer.
- File references / attachment metadata: we store references (filename, mime-type, size, and link token); binary content is not stored in the same request log blob unless the customer explicitly uploads to our storage add-on.
- KV cache: by default KV cache used for runtime attention caching is ephemeral and is not persisted to long-term logs. We do not write live KV cache contents to the auditing logs unless the customer enables "model-trace" for debugging.

Default retention windows (hosted):
- Request/response logs (including prompts and final outputs): 45 days by default for hosted customers.
- Audit logs / billing-only artifacts: 90 days for aggregated billing metadata (no PII/prompts).

How to opt out or shorten retention:
- API flag / config example: set retention.policy=ephemeral on the request or at project-level in the Console -> Data settings. This prevents storing request/response payloads (still stores minimal billing metrics).
- For Dedicated or Private deployments: retention defaults are configurable by contract; contact your Redwood AE or support to change retention windows.
- Immediate bulk purge: open a support ticket with "Data Purge" and provide the project id and timeframe. See the playbook link below for request format.

Notes and caveats:
- Backups & snapshots: standard backups may contain aggregated metadata; for hosted customers backups do not contain full prompt/response payloads beyond the 45-day window. If you need snapshot-level purging, that's an enterprise ops path.
- Masking: customers can invoke input-masking on fields (recommended for PII). Masked fields are not reconstructible from logs.

I've attached a short playbook (redwood-retention-playbook-v1.pdf) and a link to the retention matrix in Drive. If it helps, we can do a 30-minute call with our platform security engineer.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Product Manager, Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Questions on what you keep by default (KV cache, streaming, attachments)

Quick follow-up from my side — thanks Grace. Two operational clarifications our SRE team will need so we can include precise commitments in the onboarding doc for Acme: 

1) Deletion SLA: once a hosted customer raises a "Data Purge" support request, what's the expected time-to-complete for removing request/response payloads from all primary logs and indexing services? Is there any staggered replication window or eventual-consistency caveat?

2) Snapshots & backups: your note said backups do not contain full payloads — can you confirm whether nightly DB snapshots ever capture request/response payloads for hosted customers, and if so how those are handled during a purge?

Also, Lee — can you send an example project-id you want us to test against (we can do a dry-run purge to validate)?

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Lee Park <lee.park@acmeinc.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-02T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on what you keep by default (KV cache, streaming, attachments)

Karthik / Lee — answering both items and adding operational steps.

1) Deletion SLA (hosted): once we acknowledge a Data Purge ticket with the required project id and timeframe, primary log and index-level removal is completed within 72 hours. There is a short replication/consistency window where some dependent caches or analytics indices may show traces for up to 12 additional hours; we mark the purge as complete in the ticket once all indexes confirm removal. For compliance reports we provide a timestamped purge confirmation.

2) Snapshots & backups: hosted production DB snapshots do not include full prompt/response blobs by default; we only snapshot aggregated billing metadata. If a customer had enabled optional debug/model-trace (which persists additional debug dumps), those debug artifacts may be included in customer-scoped snapshots. For customers that need snapshot-level purge we have an enterprise ops path — we require an elevated request and offer a coordinated window to scrub snapshot archives.

Operational steps (recommended):
- For immediate opt-out: Console -> Project -> Data -> Retention -> set to "Ephemeral"; file a Data Purge ticket with project:id to remove the last 90 days of payloads (we'll honor shorter windows on request).
- If you need KV cache trace capture off by default: ensure model-trace is disabled (Console -> Debugging). If debugging was enabled historically, we can assist with locating and purging those traces.
- Function-call sensitive fields: use client-side masking or Redwood input-masking on the function payload fields to prevent storage of sensitive values.

I've attached the playbook (redwood-retention-playbook-v1.pdf) that includes the ticket template and a sample purge confirmation payload. Drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/retention-matrix-v2 — includes the matrix mapping artifact -> where it's stored -> how to request purge.

If you'd like, we can run a mock purge against a sample project id you provide and share the timeline and logs so your security team can verify.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Product Manager, Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference
